pages.text: Wires are strung between $(item)insulators$(), $(item)transformers$() and $(item)power pylons$(). Put an insulator on a machine or cable, take a $(item)wire coil$(), $(thing)use$() it on the first insulator and then on the second. The wire sags and must not pass through blocks. Each connection uses one coil.

$(l)Copper$(): 2,048 FE/t, up to 16 blocks. $(l)Steel$(): 16,384 FE/t, up to 24 blocks, lower loss. $(l)High-voltage$(): 131,072 FE/t, up to 48 blocks, almost lossless; only on high-voltage insulators, the transformer top and pylons. Loss grows with length.

The $(item)transformer$() stores 20,000,000 FE. The front bushing takes copper and steel wire, the top one high-voltage wire. It gives power to cables and machines at the front and takes it on the other sides except the top. Power only flows to emptier stores.
The $(item)power pylon$() is an 8-block tower with two cross-arms and four insulator strings. It takes steel and high-voltage wire; the wires run along the direction you faced when placing it.
